summary: A technically clean and geometrically disciplined Stage 1 recreation for the assigned Stage 4 88 variant. The live render matches the measured 3.71:1 silhouette, 54/46 deck-keybed allocation, exact 88-key A-to-C keyboard, continuous red chassis, and two-OLED rule. The control deck remains a schematic approximation of the reference: panel groups are much sparser, many controls are compressed or visually hidden, fine legends are difficult to read, and several control surfaces are stand-ins rather than coupled hardware state. Required tests, build checks, narrow rendering, live interactions, and console checks passed.

evidence: Live 1440x900 measurement found instrument bounds x=57.60, y=276.85, width=1324.80, height=357.09, giving a 3.710:1 ratio and 91.99% viewport width; this matches the assigned 88-key silhouette target recorded in evidence/stage1-visual-audit.md.

The render has one connected red chassis with end cheeks, a 53.7% control-deck/top-rail allocation and 46.0% keybed/bottom-rail allocation, and the exact 52 white / 36 black key geometry required for Stage 4 88.
The six section widths are correctly normalized in the live render at 13%, 21%, 15%, 9%, 21%, and 21%, but the photographed control deck is materially denser and more irregular than the candidate.

The reference image and manual pp. 9-12 show many more physical switches, LED ladders, faders, knobs, labels, and subgroup landmarks; the candidate visibly collapses Organ, Piano, Synth, and Layer Effects into sparse schematic rows with substantial empty or clipped group content.

The desktop render uses the correct dominant red chassis and slate inset panels, with black indexed knobs, silver/light fader caps, red/green indicators, cyan OLED treatments, and shaded white/black keys.

Material hierarchy is only approximate: Organ drawbars, pitch/modulation hardware, switches, and many small controls are generic CSS stand-ins rather than the distinct photographed physical forms, and the low control density weakens the reference material read.
The candidate correctly renders exactly two primary OLEDs, in Program and Synth, plus Nord Stage 4 branding and section headings; no OLED appears in Performance, Organ, Piano, or Layer Effects.
At 1440x900 most legends are only a few pixels high and hard to read, and the display contents and typography are simplified relative to the reference/manual hierarchy.

src/hardware.ts defines the assigned 88-key model, six section-specific inventories, nine Organ drawbars, LED ladder controls, Program/Synth displays, Piano selectors, Synth oscillator/filter/envelope groups, Layer Effects groups, branding, pitch stick, and modulation wheel; the live DOM exposes 52 white keys, 36 black keys, and 2 OLEDs.

The inventory is broad but approximate: the screenshot shows consolidated or hidden fine controls and does not reproduce the full photographed density and exact switch/LED/fader arrangement in the Organ, Piano, Synth, and Effects sections.

The source and live exercise cover pressed/released keys, button and LED toggles, keyboard-adjustable knob rotation, fader ranges, hover/focus treatments, and illuminated OLED state; the Live program interaction changed aria-pressed from false to true and changed the Program display to Live 1 · Stage 4.

State coverage is not fully hardware-coupled: the pitch/modulation shapes and keypad are largely decorative, and most display/meter content remains fixed apart from the limited Program/Synth display updates.

Live interaction exercised a unique Live program button, A1 white key, and Master level slider; Live program state and display feedback changed, the key pointer lifecycle completed, and Master level changed from 68 to 73 with ArrowUp.

App.tsx centralizes values and pressedKeys and HardwareControl provides reusable button, fader, and knob interaction, but several visible elements do not have meaningful behavior beyond decorative focus or local toggling.

At 390x844 the body remains exactly 390px wide with no body-level horizontal overflow; the instrument is 370x690 and the exact 88-key keybed remains visible, while the control deck is a 368px viewport over a 687px horizontally scrollable surface.

The narrow render keeps the chassis usable but exposes only the first panels initially, requires horizontal deck scrolling, and reduces legends and many controls to very small touch/read targets; the source does provide named buttons/sliders and focus-visible styles.

The implementation uses a normalized, stable-ID hardware model in src/hardware.ts, data-drives the six panels from App.tsx, and separates reusable HardwarePanel, HardwareControl, and Keyboard components.
The eight required Phase 1 feature IDs are represented in tests/feature-matrix.json, and the architecture centralizes control values and keyboard state rather than scattering unrelated panel state.
runs/gpt-5-6-luna/verifications/stage1.json reports passing pnpm test, typecheck, lint, and build checks, a built artifact, complete feature coverage, and the visual-only implementation manifest.
The live 1440x900 and 390x844 renders loaded stably, had no body clipping, and the browser console contained no error or warning entries after reload and interaction.

issues: The panel deck is substantially more schematic and less reference-faithful than the chassis and keybed, with sparse/consolidated control groups and visually clipped or hidden fine controls.
Typography and micro-labels are too small to read comfortably at desktop size, and the central OLED/control hierarchy is only an approximation of the photographed hardware.
At 390px the deck becomes horizontally scrollable and many labels/targets are very small, even though the body avoids overflow and the full keybed remains visible.

Several visible shapes such as pitch/modulation controls and the Program keypad are decorative or only minimally interactive, and display state coupling is limited beyond the exercised Live-program path.
